Each colony's figures for the whole match. The highest is highlighted where more is better; click a column heading to see how it changed over time.
How many units the colony had alive: workers, explorers and warriors together.
How fast swarms were producing new units. Split it to see workers, explorers and warriors separately.
How fast the colony was losing units, whatever the cause: combat, starvation, injuries while clearing, or being trapped.
Units born minus units lost. Above zero the colony was growing; below zero it was shrinking.
What the colony's units died of: fighting, starvation, injuries while clearing resources, being trapped with no way out, or other causes.
Units won over from other colonies minus units lost to them. Units change sides when another colony feeds them better.

How much food the colony's units were carrying inside them. Each unit is placed by how much of its food reserve is left: nearly empty (a quarter or less), low (up to half), half full (up to three quarters) or well fed. Units go looking for an inn as their reserve runs down, so a colony always has some that are low.
How healthy the colony's units were. Each unit is placed by how many of its hit points are left: critical (a quarter or less), wounded (up to half), hurt (up to three quarters) or healthy.
Units that had stopped work to find an inn. Those that are also below full health are counted as weakening.
Units inside an inn eating or inside a hospital being healed, and so not working.
Loads of food harvested by workers from food-producing resources. Inns turn food into meals.
Food sitting in the colony's buildings, ready to be served or used.
Meals the colony's inns served, to its own units and to visitors from other colonies.
Units that died because they could not find food in time.
Hit points the colony's hospitals gave back to wounded units.
Loads of every material harvested by workers. Split it to see each material.
Materials sitting in the colony's buildings. Split it to see each material.
Where delivered materials went: meals, new units, tower ammunition, new buildings or upgrades.
Materials received through markets minus materials given away.
Building work completed: new buildings, upgrades and repairs.
A score for the combined fighting power of the colony's warriors: how hard and how fast they hit.
A score for the combined firepower of the colony's defence towers.
The hit points of all the colony's units and buildings added together.
Damage the colony did to enemy units and buildings. Split it to see warriors, magic and towers.
Damage enemies did to the colony's units and buildings.
Damage dealt minus damage taken. Above zero the colony was winning its fights.
Units of this colony killed by enemies. Split it to see workers, explorers and warriors separately.
The share of shots fired by the colony's towers and explorers that hit their target.
Visits by units to schools, barracks, racetracks and swimming pools to learn a skill.
Skill levels the colony's units gained through training.
How much material stock grew in resources within 32 squares of the colony's buildings, in growth points rather than harvested loads. Split it to see how close to home they grew.
Units boxed in with no free square to step onto.
Resources removed by workers in clearing areas to make room.
The colony's prestige, earned by top-level buildings. A match with a prestige goal ends when it is reached.

How many workers were supplying each kind of building: swarms (to make new units), inns (to make meals), buildings being built or upgraded, or other buildings such as towers, schools and barracks.
How far, on average, a harvesting worker was from the building it was supplying, in map squares in a straight line.

How the workers supplying buildings divided between walking to a resource, harvesting it, carrying materials back, and delivering it or waiting for a resource they can reach. Most of it is walking, so the closer the resources, the more gets done.

How many workers were away from work to eat: walking to an inn, eating inside one, or hungry with no inn that could take them. Workers left with no inn means the colony has outgrown its inns or their food.

Your globules act on their own. You choose their jobs through buildings and flags. In this short introduction, scout a landmark, expand food supply, grow your workforce, and direct a small attack.

Select the Swarm. Set its worker target to at least 2, and its production ratios to workers only. Keep both Inns supplied while a new worker is born.
Find the enemy Swarm farther east. Use a War Flag to direct your warriors against it. Help is available if you need a reminder.

Use the minimap to move the view east and find the stone patch. Choose Exploration Flag in Flags, place it on the stone, then leave placement with the secondary mouse button. Select the flag and request 1 explorer. Flags request units; they do not move them instantly. Explorers may stop to eat.

Construction consumes wood delivered by workers. Choose Inn from the building controls (the building palette), place it in clear ground near wheat, and request 2 builders. A worker target is a request, not a count of workers already present. Keep suppliers at your existing Inn and Swarm. Any valid location counts.

Construction and everyday supply have separate worker targets. Select the finished Inn and increase its operating target. A supplier gathers wheat and carries it here. Hungry globules eat at Inns; a building with no suppliers will eventually run out. Keep the wheat patch accessible.

The Swarm consumes wheat to produce units. Set worker production to 1 and explorer and warrior production to 0. Increase the Swarm worker target to 2 or more. More suppliers can deliver wheat faster, but they compete with other jobs. Maintain food supply at both Inns.

Open Flags, choose War Flag, and place it over the enemy Swarm east of the stone. Select the flag and request up to 4 warriors. A small radius keeps them concentrated. Leave placement with the secondary mouse button before selecting the flag. If no warriors remain, produce more at the Swarm. Warriors may stop to eat; keep the Inns supplied.
Your explorer needs an assigned Exploration Flag at the eastern stone patch. Check its target and explorer count.

If you removed the new Inn, build another. Otherwise check the construction site and its worker target. Existing supply jobs may occupy your workers; keep food running while making builders available.
Select the finished new Inn. Check its worker target and watch for wheat deliveries. Workers may need time to travel or eat.

Choose Inn from Build. Place it in clear ground near wheat and confirm. Select the site and request 2 builders. A worker target is a request, not a count of workers already present. Keep the existing Inn and Swarm supplied. Any valid location counts.

Select the finished new Inn and increase its assigned-worker target. Construction and everyday supply have separate targets. A supplier gathers wheat and carries it here. Hungry globules eat at Inns; a building with no suppliers eventually runs out. Keep the wheat accessible.
